annotation.evidence_span: any TCP option it does not implement
annotation.interpretation_a: An implementation can choose to ignore *any* option it doesn't support, even standard options.
annotation.interpretation_b: An implementation can ignore options it doesn't support, but only if the option *has* a length field, as stated in the clause.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'any TCP option it does not implement' is broad and could be interpreted to include standard, required options. The clause states that the implementation should ignore the option *assuming* it has a length field, but doesn't clarify what happens if the option doesn't have a length field. This creates a potential ambiguity regarding the scope of options that can be ignored.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether the phrase 'any TCP option it does not implement' includes standard, required options. The clause could be interpreted as allowing implementations to ignore even required options, which is likely not the intent. A constraint specifying that only non-standard, optional options can be ignored would resolve the ambiguity.
